paragraphs: On Sunday at nine thirty, Tom and Lily wanted to go out to the park. But their shoes were not at the door. The children looked at the empty place by the door. Mom was making eggs on the cooker when Tom called her. "Where are the shoes?" asked Mom. "Are you sure they were here?" "I am sure," said Tom. Pip was sitting on the mat, and he looked a bit too happy. Lily looked after Pip every morning, so she knew him well.

"Let's search the house," said Mom. "Make sure that you look under things." Lily went to the living room. She was looking under the sofa when she saw a brown shoe. It was Tom's left shoe. Then she looked behind the curtain, and Tom's right shoe was there. "The shoes were hard to see," said Lily. Then a small noise came from the kitchen, and Lily went there. Pip followed her with his tail up. Lily's shoes were in the kitchen, too. One was in the box next to the fridge. One was on the chair by the window.

Tom was looking in Pip's bed when he saw a big garden glove. It was under a cushion. "Look at this," said Tom. The glove was full of small things. There was a ball, a sock, and a key. Mom laughed. "That is the key to the gate," she said. "I use it every day." "Why is the key in the glove?" asked Lily. "Pip hides things," said Mom.

Pip got a big hug. He did not look sorry at all. "Next time, Pip, please ask first," said Mom. Tom and Lily put on their shoes. At ten o'clock, the children left for the park. Pip sat on the mat and moved his tail.
